articles.title: Quote of the day by Socrates: “To Find Yourself Think for Yourself” why it stays relevant in the world of social media
articles.summary: Have you ever felt selfish thinking about yourself? What makes you happy? What do you like or dislike?
articles.body: Have you ever felt selfish thinking about yourself? What makes you happy? What do you like or dislike? These questions might seem simple but they can mean a lot for your personal journey. In a world so fast-paced with social media deciding our choices for us, people often forget that they are individuals first. Before being part of the society, before confirming what others think is best for you, people fail to think what they think for themselves. Moreover, careers are decided not by passion or the impact that a job would have on the world. The primary consideration for most people is how much money they can make and what the trending thing to do is. There is little thought put into what one would want if they were stripped off all their identities and what they actually enjoy.The existential crisis at a certain age is indicative of not knowing the most important thing in life: Yourself. Therefore, sometimes the most crucial and most interesting journeys you can take is not to some destination, it is towards knowing yourself better.Socrates, the renowned Greek philosopher, thus said, “To Find Yourself Think for Yourself”What does the quote really mean?In the modern world, most parts of our identities are provided to us at birth. Our gender, our familial ties, our social position, and even our preferences in some cases (like pink for girls and blue for boys). In this context, it feels simpler to just go on with our lives without thinking much. You just need to follow advice given by others, your parents, teachers, strangers on the internet, and you will have a life good enough to never question anything.However, there will come moments when you would doubt your decisions. On a late night at work, you might question why did you choose this life in the first place? While some might have good justifications, others wouldn’t know the answer to these questions. It is because they do not know themselves. This is what the quote conveys.The quote emphasises self-discovery and independent thinking to actually become an individual. It wants you to have courage to question your own beliefs. It goes beyond the simple likes, dislikes and talents. It is about deciding what you believe in. Your beliefs shape the decision you take, therefore, it is important that you know what is the source of your belief about certain things and why you believe it is right. Most often, it is not about being right or wrong but the thought that you might’ve put into knowing yourself.Think about it. We often inherit opinions before we even understand them. We grow up hearing what a successful person should look like, what a respectable career should be and what kind of life we should aspire to have. While advice and experience from others can guide us, accepting every opinion without questioning it can prevent us from developing our own identity.As per Socrates, “the unexamined life is not worth living.” This other quote by the Greek philosopher reflects how he believed that questioning was an essential part of gaining wisdom. He did not believe that he had all the answers, rather, he encouraged people to think that the best way to know the truth is to ask questions. He believed that any truth can be uncovered with discussion and dialogue.The relevance of this quote in today's worldIn today's world, independent thinking has become more important than ever. We live in an age where opinions are constantly presented to us through social media, online discussions, influencers and digital platforms. Due to the influencer culture, every day, someone on the internet is telling us how to dress, what to buy, where to travel, how to look and even what a successful life should mean.The problem is not that we listen to others. The problem begins when we stop listening to ourselves.Social media makes comparison of your own life with the picture presented online feel normal. The carefully curated feeds of travel pictures and loving relationships can make you feel bad about yourself. When in reality you might have more valuable relationships with your loved ones but you fail to acknowledge them. This is the lack of awareness about oneself that might affect your decisions and your personal relationships.Thus, next time, before following a trend, ask whether it genuinely interests you. Before accepting someone's opinion, think whether it makes sense for you. Before making an important decision, think about whether it reflects your values.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russell Brand's social media accounts disabled by Meta
articles.summary: It comes after the 51-year-old disgraced entertainer was sentenced to 10-and-a-half-years in prison.
articles.body:
Russell Brand's social media accounts on platforms owned by tech company Meta have been disabled.

It comes after the 51-year-old former entertainer was sentenced to 10-and-a-half-years in jail for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault earlier this week.

He was found guilty of the charges involving four women and relating to offences between 2004 and 2009.

Meta owns social media platforms including Instagram and Facebook.

Brand is currently in prison and is expected to serve seven years of his sentence behind bars before being released on licence.

On Wednesday evening, a post appeared on his X account, which remains active. "There was never a Russell Brand, according to @meta," it read.

"Thank God for @elonmusk," the message added, referring to X's owner. "Stay tuned," it concluded.

The post included what appeared to be screenshots showing Brand's Instagram account having been disabled.

Meta's community standards policy says that "in order to maintain a safe environment and empower free expression" it restricts or removes accounts that are "harmful to the community".

That includes accounts owned by convicted sex offenders.

In 2023, after a media investigation revealing allegations about Brand's behaviour - which he denies - YouTube suspended his channels from making money from adverts for "violating" its "creator responsibility policy".

At the time, the video platform said it was taking action "to protect" its users.

articles.title: DC gym shooting kills 1, injures 4; gunman dead, sources say
articles.summary: An armed assailant opened fire outside a Vida Fitness location near 15th and P Street Northwest in Washington, D.C., injuring at least five people. Law enforcement contained the suspect in a barricade, D.C. police confirmed.
articles.body: A gunman is dead after shooting himself while barricaded by police in Logan Square apartment building Thursday morning in Washington, D.C. sources told Fox News. The standoff between the gunman and police occurred after he shot somebody inside a gym at Logan Circle in Washington, D.C, and injured at least four others during the rampage, according to D.C. Metro Police and sources. During the barricade, while communicating with the suspect, police heard a gunshot in the apartment he was locked inside, D.C. MPD's interim chief of police Jeffery W. Carroll said during a Thursday morning press conference. After the gunshot, police broke down the door to find the suspect sustaining a self-inflicted gunshot wound, Carroll said. Two law enforcement officers briefed on the situation told Fox News that they were told the suspect is now dead. The suspect, a white male, also fired at officers from within the apartment building, Carroll added. NATIONAL GUARD MEMBER SHOT IN DC, POLICE CHIEF SAYS Of the four living victims who sustained injuries, one is in critical condition, according to Carroll. The shooting was reported around 8 a.m. near 15th and P streets, according to police. Carroll revealed that MPD received calls after somebody was shot inside of Vita Fitness, a local fitness chain with a location in Logan Circle. "I was at the treadmill at Vida, and five minutes in, I hear a loud bang…and this dude was on the floor, and somebody says, who was closer to the body, ’he’s dead,’" witness Anthony Mirones said. "I heard a loud bang, and then I see blood on the floor, I’m connecting the dots. Two minutes later, there’s a fire alarm, people started evacuating." Mirones added. Once outside, Mirones said gunshots were heard and "people started scattering everywhere." Vida Fitness told Fox News the location will be shut down until further notice. "We are writing to inform you that VIDA Logan Circle is temporarily closed following a shooting that occurred earlier today," Vida's prsdient Aaron Moore wrote in an alert to members. "We ask that you avoid traveling to the Logan Circle location and surrounding area until further notice. If you are currently in the vicinity, please follow all instructions from local law enforcement," the message added. "The facility will remain closed until further notice. We will provide updates as more information becomes available and it is safe and appropriate to do so. Thank you for your understanding and cooperation during this difficult time," Moore's message concluded. Carroll also told reporters that, while police are still working to ascertain the shooter's motives, they had documented a conflict he had with the homeowner's association of the apartment building in which he barricaded himself. D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser, who joined Carroll at the press conference, also weighed in. "We're devastated. Someone was killed in our city this morning in a senseless act of gun violence," Bowser told reporters. "I know many D.C. residents were awakened to this news, and were very scared, and listened to all of the directives that MPD provided, so we're grateful to them as well. MPD will continue to investigate this situation but this lone gunman has been contained," Bowser added. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) also responded to the shooting and is on scene assisting authorities, the Bureau's D.C. branch announced in a post on X. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP This is a developing story. Please check back for updates. Fox News' David Spunt contributed to this report.

articles.title: In 1972, flight attendant Vesna Vulovic fell 10,160 metres when a bomb tore her plane apart over Czechoslovakia; she was the only survivor of 28 people and still holds the record for the highest fall survived
articles.summary: On 26 January 1972, a Yugoslav Airlines flight broke apart in the sky above Czechoslovakia after an explosion tore through the aircraft.
articles.body: On 26 January 1972, a Yugoslav Airlines flight broke apart in the sky above Czechoslovakia after an explosion tore through the aircraft. Among the 28 people on board, only one person lived: 23-year-old flight attendant Vesna Vulovic. According to Guinness World Records, she fell from an altitude of 10,160 metres, or 33,333 feet, and survived without a parachute, a feat that still stands as the record for the highest fall survived.The story sounds almost impossible, yet it is documented in official accident records, contemporary reporting and later accounts of her life. Vulovic was found amid wreckage on a snow-covered mountainside near Srbska Kamenice, injured so severely that doctors did not expect her to live. She spent years recovering, but eventually returned to work and became one of the most remarkable survivors in aviation history.A routine flight becomes a disasterVulovic was working as a Jugoslavenski Aerotransport hostess aboard a Douglas DC-9 flying from Stockholm to Belgrade. The aircraft had stopped in Copenhagen before continuing its journey, and it was during this stopover that investigators suspected an explosive device had been placed on board.Shortly after the plane left Copenhagen, an explosion ripped through the aircraft at high altitude. The official accident report stated that the blast tore the DC-9 apart in midair, scattering wreckage across a remote, wooded area of Czechoslovakia, now the Czech Republic.All 27 other passengers and crew members died in the disaster. Vulovic was the sole survivor, a fact that turned an already tragic aviation accident into one of the most extraordinary survival stories ever recorded.Why she survived the fallInvestigators believed that Vulovic was trapped by a food cart in the tail section of the aircraft as it plunged toward the ground. That section of the plane eventually landed in a heavily forested, snow-covered mountainside, and the terrain is thought to have softened the impact enough to give her a chance of survival.The snow, trees and angled slope may have acted as a crude but vital cushion. Rather than striking a flat, hard surface, the tail section appears to have come down through terrain that absorbed some of the force of the impact.It is important to understand that surviving such a fall was not simply a matter of luck. The position of the wreckage, the freezing conditions, the way the aircraft broke apart and the immediate rescue all played a role. Even so, the outcome remains exceptionally rare, which is why Guinness World Records continues to recognise it as the highest fall survived without a parachute.Found alive in the wreckageVulovic was discovered by Bruno Honke, a local woodsman who heard her screaming in the darkness while debris continued to fall around him. He found her alive in the wreckage and she was rushed to hospital for emergency treatment.Her injuries were catastrophic. She had suffered a fractured skull, two crushed vertebrae, a broken pelvis, several broken ribs and fractures in both legs. After arriving at hospital, she fell into a coma, and accounts differ on how long it lasted, with Guinness World Records reporting 27 days and the BBC reporting 10 days.For a time, she was temporarily paralysed from the waist down. Doctors were uncertain whether she would walk again, let alone return to any form of normal life.A long and painful recoveryVulovic spent 16 months in hospital after the crash, undergoing extensive treatment and rehabilitation. Her body had been shattered by the impact, and the road back was long, painful and uncertain.Against the odds, she made a near-full recovery. Although she did not return to flying, she eventually went back to work for the airline in a desk-based role.She later described the experience in simple, striking terms. “I was broken, and the doctors put me back together again,” she told The New York Times in 2008. “Nobody ever expected me to live this long.”A record that still standsIn 1985, Vulovic entered the Guinness Book of Records for surviving the highest fall without a parachute. Guinness World Records officially lists the record as 10,160 metres, set on 26 January 1972 over Srbska Kamenice in what was then Czechoslovakia.The record has never been broken. While other people have survived falls from extreme heights, none has been documented as surviving a fall from a greater altitude without a parachute.There has been some debate over the exact altitude at which the aircraft broke apart. In 2009, a journalistic investigation suggested that the plane may have begun an emergency descent before disintegrating, meaning the actual fall distance could have been lower than the official figure. However, even one of the journalists involved acknowledged that the evidence was circumstantial.The mystery of the bombingThe suspected bombing was never fully solved. Investigators believed that a device may have been planted on the aircraft during its stopover in Copenhagen, but no one was ever arrested and no conclusive proof was ever established.The lack of certainty has followed the story for decades. What is known is that the aircraft broke apart in flight, that 27 people died and that Vulovic alone survived. The question of who was responsible, and why, remains unanswered.Life after the crashVulovic became a national figure in Serbia, where her survival story earned her a level of fame few ordinary citizens ever experience. She used that visibility to speak on political issues and became known for her opposition to nationalism.She was dismissed from her airline job in 1990 after taking part in protests against President Slobodan Milosevic. Even after leaving the airline, she continued to speak out on political matters for another two decades.Despite everything she had been through, Vulovic continued to fly as a passenger. She once said that people often wanted to sit next to her on planes, perhaps drawn by the extraordinary story behind her survival.A survivor unlike any otherVesna Vulovic died in December 2016 at the age of 66. Her death was reported by Serbian state television, though the cause was not immediately known at the time.Her story endures because it sits at the edge of what seems possible. A young flight attendant, caught in an explosion at cruising altitude, fell from more than 10,000 metres and lived. The record she holds is not just a statistic. It is a reminder of how fragile life can be, and how occasionally, against every expectation, it survives.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Migrant caravan sets out from southern Mexico bound for US after midterms
articles.summary: Many migrants stranded in southern Mexico say the Democrats’ win in Congress has given them new hope of entering the US.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has warned Mexico that it must stop a group of migrants travelling through the country towards the US border or face a doubling of tariffs.

“Huge CARAVANS are forming and beginning their illegal march through Mexico. Many of the people in these Caravans are those that various countries don’t want,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Thursday. The president said that a “perceived loss” by his Republican Party in last week’s midterm elections had emboldened the migrants, and that he was putting the incoming Democratic governor of the border state of Texas on notice about the issue.

Republicans lost control of the House of Representatives and the Senate in the midterm elections, with Democrats flipping multiple seats in both chambers of Congress.

More than a thousand migrants began marching on Tuesday through southern Mexico in a caravan, encouraged by last week’s Democratic victory in the elections, as Mexican authorities blocked a second, smaller group from trying to reach the US.

The caravan, called “God With Us”, was en route on Wednesday after setting off the day before from Tapachula, near the Guatemalan border, according to the Reuters news agency.

A Chiapas state government source estimated about 1,500 people were taking part, including many families, with parents carrying small children in their arms, in strollers or on their shoulders.

The migrants, mostly from Central America, said they aim first to reach Mexico City, more than 1,000km (621 miles) away, a journey likely to take at least several weeks, to seek help from the Mexican government and protection from detention.

Tapachula is a key transit point for migrants heading to the US , and thousands have become stranded there because of US entry restrictions and deportations, with few jobs, little healthcare and limited access to schools.

Caravans are common, but many migrants said the Democrats’ victory in congressional elections, in which voters delivered a rebuke of President Trump in part for his immigration policies, gave them new hope.

Among the unusual victories by Democrats was the governorship of Texas, which went to Gina Hinojosa, a woman of Mexican-American descent, and the first Latina to lead the state.

“There might be a light at the end of the tunnel, a way for us to get in,” said Cesar Sandoval, a 47-year-old Nicaraguan who was deported from the US a few months ago. “We believe the Democrats will help us,” he added.

Local news footage showed officers positioned across a road, and the migrants ran as they were surrounded. About 40 were detained, according to reports from Tapachula.

The larger group of about 1,000 had crossed on Sunday evening without resistance. It is the third caravan to try to reach the US since September, the AFP said. The other two were broken up before leaving Chiapas, and their members were given temporary stay permits.

“As long as Trump remains president, the deportations will not stop,” said Ivan Porraz, a researcher at the College of the Southern Border.

articles.title: Cow rescued after falling into swimming pool in Cornwall
articles.summary: It is believed the cow wandered into the garden and then walked on to the pool cover which gave way.
articles.body:
A cow was rescued by fire fighters after escaping and falling into a garden swimming pool.

The 600kg (1,322lb) cow fell into the 1.2m (3ft 11ins) deep pool in a garden in Coverack, Cornwall, fire crews said.

Two appliances from St Keverne were called at 01:18 GMT on Wednesday and secured the animal using ropes before using a portable pump to reduce the water level in the pool by 50%.

Cornwall Fire and Rescue Service said once the water was low enough the animal was led to safety and left in the care of the farmer.

Firefighters said they thought the cow had wandered into the garden before walking on to the pool cover which gave way underneath it.

articles.title: A woman called off her wedding weeks before the ceremony; a London family court later ordered her to return seven jewellery items worth £67,942 to her former fiancé
articles.summary: The Central Family Court in London has ordered a woman to return seven pieces of jewellery worth £67,942 to her former fiancé after finding that she had
articles.body: The Central Family Court in London has ordered a woman to return seven pieces of jewellery worth £67,942 to her former fiancé after finding that she had removed them from his apartment without his knowledge or consent. The couple had agreed to marry, but the woman called off the wedding scheduled for 15 May 2024. She denied that they were engaged and disputed the man's claims about the jewellery.However, District Judge Ashworth found that the engagement had taken place and that the woman had removed the items, either keeping them or disposing of them.According to RI v NG [2025] EWFC 9 (B), the court ordered her to return the jewellery within seven days of the final order being approved or pay the value of any items not returned.Judge rejects woman's denial after examining engagement and wedding evidenceThe couple met in June 2023 and were in a relationship by at least January 2024. The man, identified in the judgment as Mr RI, said they agreed to marry in February 2024, with the wedding scheduled for 15 May. The woman, Ms NG, ended the relationship on 30 April. She denied that they had been engaged and said he had planned the wedding without her consent. The judge accepted the man’s account.The ruling referred to the engagement ring, photographs shared on Instagram describing him as her ‘future husband’ and an email to an insurance broker calling him her fiancé, arrangements with Chelsea Old Town Hall and a meeting about a pre-nuptial agreement. The judge concluded that the woman had accepted his proposal and that the wedding was later called off by her.Man's £67,942 jewellery claim included expensive rings and necklacesThe man said he had bought the jewellery as an engagement ring and wedding gifts for his former partner. He stressed that his claim did not include items he accepted he had given to her. The seven items included jewellery supported by invoices, an insurance valuation and other evidence considered by the court in the proceedings. The judge accepted that he had bought items from a seller for $20,500, with an insurance or replacement valuation of £37,500.The court also accepted his evidence about a £20,000 purchase of an eternity ring and diamond tennis necklace. Other items included a wedding ring bought in Spain, diamond hoop earrings valued at £5,000 and a gold and diamond necklace valued at £2,500.Court favours man's evidence over woman's claims about missing jewelleryThe woman disputed the existence, ownership or whereabouts of several pieces. She said some jewellery already belonged to her and that she did not know about other items. The judge found the man to be a reliable witness overall, despite some uncertainty when recalling details. The judge did not find the woman reliable, citing inconsistencies and explanations that were considered implausible.The court accepted that the man had searched extensively for the missing jewellery and found no evidence of a break-in or burglary at his home. He had reported the matter to the police, who were waiting for the outcome of the court proceedings before deciding whether to take further action.Court orders former partner to return jewellery items within seven daysThe court found that the woman had removed the seven items and retained them or disposed of them. The judge found the other items had not yet been gifted and were intended as wedding gifts. For the engagement ring, the judge held the presumption that it was a gift was rebutted because she ended the engagement. The judgment directed her to return the items within seven days of a final order being approved.If she does not return any item, she must pay the man the value of that item as claimed by him and found by the court. The direction covered all seven pieces of jewellery. The judge also noted that neither party had addressed the question of costs and invited them to agree on the wording of the order and any costs issue.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available court records published by The National Archives. The Times of India has not independently verified the details of the relationship, the jewellery purchases, or the court proceedings mentioned in the article.You use AI every day. articles.title: Iran's shadow operations stretch across Europe as chilling spy convictions expose Tehran's reach
articles.summary: Two Iranian men convicted of spying in Britain as France accuses the IRGC of cyberattacks and UAE officials warn of Iranian sleeper cells abroad.
articles.body: Two Iranian men were convicted in Britain on Thursday of spying on journalists and critics of Tehran, the latest case raising alarm over Iranian operations beyond the Middle East, as France accuses the IRGC of unprecedented cyberattacks and a senior UAE official warns of Iranian sleeper cells abroad. The developments come as the Trump administration continues its campaign of economic pressure against Tehran while leaving the door open to diplomatic negotiations, raising questions about how Iran's overseas intelligence networks and alleged covert activities might factor into any future agreement. A jury at Woolwich Crown Court in London found Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, guilty of engaging in conduct likely to assist a foreign intelligence service after prosecutors said they carried out surveillance of journalists and other individuals critical of the Iranian government, according to Reuters. IRAN TURNS CITIZENS INTO INFORMANTS AS CHILLING CRACKDOWN SPREADS BEYOND ITS BORDERS The targets included journalists working for Iran International, a London-based Persian-language news outlet critical of Tehran, and a prominent figure associated with UK Lawyers for Israel. According to prosecutors, the surveillance operation took place between August 2024 and March 2025 and involved visits to locations associated with the targets, photographs, videos and online research. Sepahvand was also convicted of engaging in preparatory conduct with the intention of committing serious violence against a person in Britain, while Manesh was acquitted of that charge and a third defendant was cleared of all charges. British authorities described the case as the first convictions of Iranian nationals under the National Security Act of 2023, warning that the verdicts underscored an ongoing threat from Iranian intelligence operations. Iran has denied involvement. Similar concerns have emerged in the United States. Just two days before the British verdicts, the U.S. Justice Department announced terrorism charges against three alleged Iranian-backed operatives accused of involvement in nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks across Europe and the United States. The three men allegedly supported Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Kata'ib Hezbollah, targeting Jewish communities and plotting an attack on RAF Fairford, a British air base housing American military personnel, according to the Nov. 10 indictment. Prosecutors allege that one defendant, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, continued coordinating terrorist activities through coded messages while imprisoned in New York. The network was also allegedly involved in planning an attack on a Manhattan synagogue. FRENCH SUPERMARKETS FACE MILLIONS IN LOSSES AFTER CYBERATTACK HITS REFRIGERATORS NATIONWIDE In France, authorities on Monday accused Iran's IRGC of orchestrating a major cyberattack against the country's food supply infrastructure. According to a Nov. 9 report by France's Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre, Iranian-linked hackers targeted refrigeration controllers at approximately 700 retail locations across France on Oct. 11 and 12. Investigators said the attackers remotely altered defrost settings, causing refrigeration equipment to reach abnormally high temperatures, spoiling significant quantities of food and triggering at least 15 reported fire outbreaks. The operation affected major supermarket chains, including Carrefour, Leclerc and Intermarché, as well as other businesses in the food industry. French investigators attributed the operation to Shahid Kaveh, a cyber-offensive unit operating under the IRGC's electronic and cyber command. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot described the attack as unprecedented in its scale and aggression, while authorities announced plans to pursue European sanctions against those responsible. Iran's Foreign Ministry rejected what it described as baseless and malicious allegations in a statement issued Tuesday strongly condemning the "persistent practice" of directing accusations toward Tehran. 'KEEP A LOW PROFILE': STATE DEPARTMENT WARNS AMERICANS OVERSEAS THEY COULD BE TARGETED The European cases echo warnings from the Gulf, where officials have raised concerns that Iran's regional operations extend beyond missiles, drones and armed proxy groups. Dr. Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, chairman of the Defense, Interior and Foreign Affairs Committee of the UAE's Federal National Council, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview that Iranian-linked sleeper cells were operating both within the region and elsewhere. "They created these sleeping cells in the region and also in other places," Al Nuaimi said. "We were fortunate to find out about these cells, to act and to implement the law, our law, the UAE law, against them." Al Nuaimi previously disclosed during an Oct. 15 briefing that hundreds of suspected Iranian sleeper-cell members had been arrested in the UAE, including individuals he said helped direct Iranian missile and drone attacks against the country. Speaking separately to Fox News Digital, Al Nuaimi argued that negotiations with Tehran should address not only its nuclear program and regional proxies, but also covert networks operating in other countries. "This is where it should be part of the negotiation with the Iranians: you have to stop not only the proxies that we know, but also using these sleeping cells in other countries," he said. Beyond the criminal investigations, Iranian-American journalist and foreign policy analyst Lisa Daftari described the personal toll of what she believes to be Iranian intelligence operations on U.S. soil. In an earlier interview with Fox News Digital, Daftari said she had been followed in Los Angeles and New York, repeatedly hacked and approached in person. She said the FBI informed her that she was on a list of potential Iranian regime targets after hackers gained access to her accounts. "The message they want to send is very clear, that we know where you are, we can reach you," she said. TRUMP'S FIRST IRAN WAR ESCALATION POST-MIDTERM LOSSES SEEKS TO CHOKE OFF TEHRAN’S TRADE In a joint declaration issued Wednesday following a meeting in Paris, G7 foreign ministers expressed grave concern about Iranian involvement in violent plots targeting people and territory in their countries. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking to reporters following the G7 meeting on Tuesday, accused Tehran of being responsible for much of the instability across the Middle East. "They are behind all the instability in the region; they are the source of instability in the region," Rubio said, referring to Iran's support for armed groups, including Hezbollah, Hamas and the Houthis. Rubio argued that the Trump administration's economic pressure campaign was significantly weakening the Iranian government and reducing its ability to finance activities abroad, including terrorism and cyber operations. He said Washington remained open to diplomacy but would not accept what he described as unrealistic Iranian demands. The G7 declaration also pledged to continue coordinating economic and political measures designed to constrain Tehran's ability to destabilize countries both inside and outside the Middle East. The British convictions, French cyberattack findings and UAE allegations involve different types of activity, and no evidence has been presented establishing that they formed part of a single coordinated operation. articles.title: India can't fight its next war with 17 separate commands, says ex-Navy chief Admiral Sunil Lanba
articles.summary: India needs integrated theatre commands because its armed forces can no longer plan and fight wars service by service, former Navy chief Admiral Sunil
articles.body: India needs integrated theatre commands because its armed forces can no longer plan and fight wars service by service, former Navy chief Admiral Sunil Lanba (retd) has said. He described the Indian Air Force's reluctance to divide its assets as the main obstacle."We cannot have 17 independent commands, none of them co-located," Lanba told TOI's Defence HQ podcast. “The need of the hour is joint planning and joint execution." With AI shortening decision cycles, he said, separate services operating in separate environments is "not going to run".Lanba headed the Navy from 2016 to 2019 and chaired the Chiefs of Staff Committee. Asked why the reform is needed when Operation Sindoor succeeded without it, he pointed to Pulwama. A year before the 2019 attack, he said, he had the operations directorates of the three services draw up a joint plan for a "contingency short of war", which was passed down to all commands. "That helped us when Pulwama happened, and finally it led to the Balakot incident," he said. A theatre command, with one joint commander over Army, Navy and Air Force components, would be "much more effective".The IAF's objections, Lanba said, "can all be worked out". Strategic assets should stay with the Air Force, he argued, while tactical platforms such as attack helicopters should go to the Army. "I know the Air Force guys will pan me for saying all this."The Navy, about one-fourteenth the size of the Army, need not fear being subsumed, he said, since the maritime theatre would remain its own. He would prefer two maritime theatres, one for each seaboard, but called the single one now proposed "fair enough".The plan for Northern, Western and Maritime theatres, submitted in April, still awaits Cabinet Committee on Security clearance. IAF chief A P Singh said in August that the force is not against theaterisation but wants a gradual rollout.On submarines, Lanba said a 1999 plan for 24 conventional boats in 30 years has "suffered great delays". That plan was later revised to 18 conventional and six nuclear-powered attack submarines. He faulted the 2015 decision to bring in a private shipyard for Project 75I, cleared in principle in 2007, when Mazagon Dock and Visakhapatnam already had submarine lines. The deal still awaits final approval. "All delays lead to costs," he said. On conventional versus nuclear attack submarines, he said: "It can't be either. It has to be both."The Navy's last sanctioned force level, from 1964, envisaged about 140 ships built around three aircraft carriers, he said. Three remains the ideal, so that one can be in refit while two operate in the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal. Gaps are costly, he said, because carrier flying, where every landing is "a controlled crash", is hard to relearn once lost.Lanba also called the September 15 collision between INS Kolkata and Pakistan's PNS Hunain in the Arabian Sea "most unprofessional". He said the Pakistani commanding officer had breached agreed confidence-building measures. Pakistan has blamed the Indian destroyer.

articles.title: In 1992, Kurt Cobain gave Mark Lanegan a smashed, band-signed Fender; 31 years later, it sold for nearly $600,000
articles.summary: Discover the remarkable story of Kurt Cobain's smashed Fender guitar that sold for nearly $600,000 at auction. This iconic instrument, gifted to Mark Lanegan in 1992, showcases Cobain's legacy and the enduring impact of Nirvana's music.
articles.body: Kurt Cobain remained a name inseparable from the annals of rock and roll history. A divisive figure, he was endeared to his generation and inspired a devoted following. Older rock audiences did not always understand his songwriting, defined by criticism of apathy and hypocrisy. According to The Washington Post, the battered guitar, with a broken neck and a handwritten greeting, went to auction in May 2023. The Fender Stratocaster had passed from the Nirvana singer to Mark Lanegan in 1992 during the band’s North American tour. Years later, Julien’s Auctions sold it for $596,900, against an estimated value of $60,000 to $80,000, per Julien’s Auctions.A gift between rock iconsThe guitar was a left-handed, black-and-white Fender Stratocaster made in Japan, dating to 1990. Its body bore silver-marker signatures from Nirvana’s drummer Dave Grohl and bassist Krist Novoselic. Cobain’s inscription read: “Hell-o Mark! Love, Your Pal, Kurdt Kobain/ Washed up rockstar”.The guitar’s recipient was Mark Lanegan, the singer-songwriter of Screaming Trees and a close friend and musical collaborator of Cobain. Their work crossed over on music recordings before the gift. Cobain sang on “Down in the Dark” and played guitar on “Where Did You Sleep Last Night”, both on Lanegan’s 1990 solo album, The Winding Sheet. Lanegan also contributed to the lyrics of “Something in the Way,” which appeared on Nirvana’s seminal album Nevermind. The two had reportedly planned to work on an album titled “The Jury,” but the plan never came to fruition.According to Julien’s Auctions, Cobain handed over the guitar as a gift to Lanegan during 1992, at a North American leg of Nirvana’s tour. It came with a signed provenance letter from the previous owner, Tony Palmer. Cobain’s guitar was distinguishable from the standard Stratocaster. The instrument had a white pickguard, Gotoh tuners and a Hot Rails humbucker in the bridge position, alongside two single-coil pickups. Three original white control knobs and a five-way selector switch were present on the body, together with a vintage-style tremolo bridge. Its solid alder body had a double-cutaway shape, while the maple neck was bolted on; the rosewood fingerboard had small clay dot markers. The words “Boddah Lives” were scratched on the neck plate; Boddah was the name of Cobain’s childhood imaginary friend.Unplayable yet priceless Cobain had probably repaired it after smashing it. Its modifications showed signs of extended use, which led the auction house to determine that he continued playing it after the damage.There were two other black Fender guitars associated with Cobain’s instrument destruction: One, displayed at Seattle’s Museum of Pop Culture. It had a white bumper sticker that said: “Vandalism: Beautiful as a Rock / in a Cop’s Face”. Another was broken during the studio recording of “Endless, Nameless”, the hidden track on Nevermind, which played after a long pause following “Something in the Way”. Parts of that guitar had also been displayed at the museum.The Stratocaster’s rosewood fingerboard and neck were broken; the damage extended from the fifth fret to the position of the fourth tuner. Three Gotoh tuners remained attached to the surviving headstock. The pickups and electronics still worked, making the body functional, but the damaged neck meant the guitar could not be played.It was offered in a black Fender hard case marked “Abort Christ” in white lettering. The sale was part of a three-day “Music Icons” auction at Hard Rock Cafe in New York. The event included more than 1,200 items connected to musicians such as Whitney Houston, Michael Jackson, Elvis Presley and Bob Dylan. Darren Julien, the president and CEO of Julien’s Auctions, opened the bidding at $15,000 as per the Post. The $596,900 result was far above the auction house’s estimate. This followed other sales of Cobain instruments, the Los Angeles Times reported in 2023, including his acoustic Martin D-18 E, used during Nirvana’s “MTV Unplugged” performance, which sold for $6 million in 2020. Another was a 1969 Fender Mustang from the “Smells Like Teen Spirit” video, which fetched $4.5 million in 2022.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger tells Jimmy Kimmel he still considers himself a Republican
articles.summary: Former California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger told Jimmy Kimmel he's still a Republican, citing Ronald Reagan as the kind of GOP leader he admires.
articles.body: Actor and former California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger declared on Wednesday that he’s still a Republican despite disagreements with the modern GOP. The "Terminator" actor, who served as California’s last Republican governor from 2003-2011, appeared on ABC’s "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" and was asked by the liberal late-night host if he was still a member of his longtime party. "I’m a Republican, absolutely," Schwarzenegger said. Kimmel shot back, "What does that mean anymore?" SETH MEYERS, JOHN OLIVER TELL JIMMY KIMMEL HE'S THEIR 'BULLETPROOF VEST' WHEN IT COMES TO TRUMP Schwarzenegger said a traditional Republican "is someone that admires the Republican Party for having freed the slaves," but was interrupted by Kimmel insisting, "They don’t get credit for that anymore. Come on now." Despite Kimmel’s interjection, Schwarzenegger continued to list why he admires the GOP. "This is what I’m about… [they’ve] given those slaves American citizenship, and given them the rights to vote, it’s Republicans," Schwarzenegger said as Kimmel interrupted him again. "This sounds like all the opposite things that the Republican Party stands for now," Kimmel said. "Doesn’t it?" Schwarzenegger said, "That doesn't mean that I have to change my philosophy," citing former President and fellow California Gov. Ronald Reagan for his efforts to improve air quality and former President Richard Nixon for establishing the Environmental Protection Agency. BLUE WAVE NEARLY SWALLOWED SOME OF AMERICA'S REDDEST STATES AS ELECTION DATA EXPOSES GOP'S CLOSE CALLS "Those are the kind of Republicans that used to go and work together with the Democrats and got things done," Schwarzenegger said. "This is the kind of Republican that I am." Kimmel, who has spent years mocking President Donald Trump on a nightly basis, told Schwarzenegger he was the "only one of them" remaining. "No, I don’t think I’m the only one left. But look, this doesn’t mean that we should give up. The bottom line is, we have just seen now what some people call the blue wave… now the Democrats go in and they have the majority," Schwarzenegger said. "It has been going back and forth for the last 20 years, and what happened in the last 20 years? None of them did true immigration reform… none of them participated in reducing our debt, none of them created a healthcare system where everyone is insured," Schwarzenegger added. Kimmel stopped him and pointed to Obamacare, but Schwarzenegger dismissed it as a "good attempt" that was essentially "bogus." "If the Democrats do something by themselves, or if the Republicans do something by themselves, it’s bogus," Schwarzenegger said. "What you have to do is, the Democrats and the Republicans have to work together like we did when I was governor of California… that’s the only way you can accomplish something." TRUMP ADMIN CRACKS DOWN ON ESTIMATED $10 BILLION IN OBAMACARE FRAUD, BOOTS MILLIONS FROM ROLLS The Austrian-born Schwarzenegger then called for elected officials to serve the public, not their party. Kimmel later asked whether Trump had reached out to Schwarzenegger for advice during his first presidential campaign in 2016. "We talked to each other several times, because we had a good relationship, we were very good friends, and he asked me if I would go and endorse him, campaign with him. I said to him, ‘Donald, I like to be your friend… but it happens to be that there are certain things that you stand for, that you’re talking about to people out there, that I don’t believe in,’" Schwarzenegger said. articles.title: TPUSA students warn campus hostility toward conservatives is growing after Texas university attack
articles.summary: Footage shows a caped suspect hurling an American flag and swinging a cane at Turning Point USA members on the University of Texas at Tyler campus.
articles.body: Turning Point USA (TPUSA) members involved in a violent confrontation at the University of Texas at Tyler say growing hostility toward conservative voices on college campuses is threatening open dialogue. "The fact that we're there for open conversation on campus, it's sad that that's something that would make him be so aggressive towards us," TPUSA field representative Janae Jenson told "Fox & Friends" on Thursday. Jenson, who appeared alongside fellow TPUSA member Davis Thrower, said the suspect, identified as Ciro Tomlian, 19, a former UT Tyler student, repeatedly approached their display, insulting the group before the confrontation turned physical. TURNING POINT USA EVENT AT UNIVERSITY OF NEW MEXICO ENDS WITH TWO ARRESTS AND A STRING OF CHARGES Jenson said the incident caught her off guard, particularly because she described UT Tyler as a "small" and "mostly conservative" campus, but she suggested the confrontation reflects a broader pattern of hostility toward conservative students. "Our students face threats of violence and mean words all the time on the daily. So, I mean something like this is bound to happen eventually," she said. Video shows Tomlian wearing a cape and a round-brimmed hat as he throws an American flag on the ground and swings a cane at a group of people. TPUSA members can be heard urging him to stop and warning that police were nearby. "I think the media and interacting online has radicalized a lot of individuals," Thrower said, when asked about the confrontation. UTAH STUDENT CITED AFTER PHYSICAL ALTERCATION WITH COLLEGE REPUBLICAN CAUGHT ON CAMERA "I also believe that we have a major health crisis, mental health crisis within our nation that is not properly addressed," Thrower added. A Gallup survey published in December 2025 found that 30% of adults ages 18 to 29 said it is sometimes acceptable to use violence to achieve a political goal. Asked about the Gallup findings, Thrower said some people fail to understand that physically hurting others because of political disagreements is unacceptable. "They hear something they don't like and they don't understand that it's not acceptable to lash out and physically hurt people," he said. University of Texas at Tyler police arrested Tomlian following the incident. According to university officials and local reports, he faces two counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and one count of assault causing bodily injury, stemming from accusations that he struck people at the TPUSA event with a cane. articles.title: Fourteen dead after truck loses control in 23-vehicle crash in UAE
articles.summary: Authorities say the driver lost control and collided with 23 vehicles including five trucks in the traffic.
articles.body:
Fourteen people have been killed and dozens injured after a truck driver lost control and hit several vehicles in Fujairah, in the United Arab Emirates, the interior ministry has said.

The accident involved 23 vehicles including five trucks, and happened at the entrance of the eastern emirate in "slow-moving traffic" just before midnight, the ministry added in a statement.

The impact caused "the truck to catch fire and the blaze to spread to several other vehicles, resulting in a heavy loss of life", it said.

Thirty people were injured and taken to hospital, Fujairah Police said, adding that DNA tests are being used to identify the bodies of the victims.

Some of them were Emirati nationals, the police added.

The Indian consulate in the UAE said its citizens were also among the deceased, and said it has reached out to "bereaved families" and is working with the local authorities to provide assistance and support.

Officials said the truck collided with another vehicle before overturning and striking others that had stopped due to "slow-moving traffic" on the street.

Emergency services, including the police, paramedics and civil defence teams rushed to the scene to extinguish the fire, transfer the injured to hospitals and secure the site, where specialist teams remain.

Both the interior ministry and police expressed their deepest condolences and heartfelt sympathy to the families of the deceased, and wished a speedy recovery to those injured.

Half of the injured were discharged from hospital after receiving treatment, while the rest remain in medical care.

The authorities said their nationalities are Emirati, Omani, Indian, Brazilian, Pakistani, Jordanian, and Egyptian.

articles.title: Parliament date set for 'summer of sex' campaign debate
articles.summary: South Derbyshire MP Samantha Niblett is campaigning for lifelong sex education.
articles.body:
An MP has been given a date for a House of Commons debate following her campaign calling for lifelong sex education.

Dubbed the "summer of sex", the campaign was launched to push education about consent, respect and healthy relationships, with the aim of preventing abuse and violence, but has received a mixed response in Westminster.

Samantha Niblett has previously said she also planned a separate event to display a number of sex toys and sex education aids in Parliament as part of the campaign. However, this is unlikely to take place until the new year.

The backbench debate is due to take place in Parliament on 26 November, it has been confirmed.

The South Derbyshire MP applied in March for the debate, but said she faced a "longer wait" for it to be granted because she wanted it to take place in the main chamber, rather than a lower-profile venue such as Westminster Hall.

"I wanted it to be in the main chamber as the gravity of the topic warrants the surroundings that most people think of when they think of Parliament debates," she said in a Facebook post.

She also said she had been "astounded" by the support she had received for the campaign, which was initially met with reluctance.

"Today, I was finally granted my debate, which will take place on Thursday 26 November, when I'll deliver my speech based on the huge journey I've been on these past seven to eight months, and making some initial recommendations to government," she said.

"But what is clear is this is just the beginning, and in light of recent events this campaign has never been more important."

In a session of Prime Minister's Questions in September, Prime Minister Andy Burnham agreed to meet Niblett on the issue and praised her for "raising important issues that others won't talk about".

He added: "It's very clear to me that her summer was more exciting than mine."

MPs who are not in government can apply for backbench debates on a topic of their choice to a dedicated cross-party committee.

The debate is opened by the MP who requested it, and other backbenchers from any party can contribute.

A government minister and the opposition frontbench also respond with their views on the issue.

articles.title: Small units seek relief from Pb govt wage rule
articles.summary: Punjab mandates wage payments via banks/e-modes; Ludhiana hosiery and dyeing bodies seek exemption for small units, urging flexibility for cash advances.
articles.body: Ludhiana: A Punjab govt move requiring factories and establishments to pay wages only through cheque, direct bank credit or electronic modes has put Ludhiana’s small-industry sector on edge, with hosiery and dyeing associations arguing that a blanket ban on cash payments could make it difficult to provide workers small advances for everyday emergencies.The Knitwear Club and Punjab Dyers Association have approached the state govt seeking a rethink of the notification, particularly for cottage, micro and small units. While backing digital payment of regular wages, they have sought flexibility for cash advances that workers frequently take for food, rent, medicines, transportation and other immediate needs.The issue assumes significance in Ludhiana, where Knitwear Club chairman Vinod Thapar said there were around 10,000 hosiery units, a substantial number of them operating in the cottage, household, micro and small-scale segments.In a representation to the state labour minister, Thapar said many workers in these units were unskilled, semi-skilled or migrants and depended on daily or weekly earnings. Small advances were frequently provided by employers and subsequently adjusted against wages.The industry maintains that routing every such small payment through banks or electronic modes could cause practical difficulties, particularly where workers have limited access to digital payment facilities. Frequent small transactions would also have to be reconciled by establishments with limited administrative infrastructure, it said.Thapar said the industry was not opposing digital wage payments. Instead, it wanted the govt to distinguish between regular wages and interim advances given to workers against their earnings.Industry representatives also fear that removing this flexibility could make it more difficult for small units to retain workers, particularly when employees require money at short notice.The Punjab Dyers Association has separately written to the chief minister and labour minister, raising questions over the notification. The association maintained that the Code on Wages provides for different modes of wage payment and sought a review of the state’s order.It has sought withdrawal of the notification or exemptions for seasonal industries such as hosiery, dyeing, knitting, garments and processing.As an alternative, the association has proposed a 70:30 or 80:20 formula, under which 70% to 80% of wages could be transferred to workers’ bank accounts while the remaining 20% to 30% could be paid in cash depending on workers’ requirements and consent.The association has warned that it would approach the Punjab and Haryana High Court through a writ petition if the govt does not take steps within 15 days.Industry bodies have also suggested allowing limited cash advances against written acknowledgements and proper records. articles.title: Big reshuffle at civic body, senior team recast
articles.summary: Ludhiana MC sees major reshuffle as Punjab govt transfers key engineering and administrative officers; new municipal secretary appointed, building branch head vacant.
articles.body: Ludhiana: Days after Damanjit Singh Mann took charge as municipal commissioner, the state govt has carried out a sweeping reshuffle in Ludhiana MC, shifting several senior officers and bringing in new faces in a shake-up that has substantially recast the civic body’s engineering and administrative wings.The engineering branch has seen some of the biggest changes, with four superintending engineers (SEs) transferred out of Ludhiana. Praveen Kumar Singla and Sham Lal Gupta have been posted to Jalandhar, Ranjit Singh to Patiala and Harkiranpal Singh to Moga.Sandeep Singh Romana, earlier posted in Bathinda, has been brought to Ludhiana, while Rajneesh Dogra from Jalandhar and Mandeep Singh from Kapurthala are also among officers being posted to the city.The administrative set-up, too, has undergone a shake-up. Assistant commissioner Neeraj Jain has been transferred to Barnala and Jasdev Singh Sekhon to Amritsar, while a new officer is expected to join Ludhiana MC shortly.The transfers of joint commissioners Amanpreet Singh and Vineet Kumar have further altered the senior administrative team. Joint commissioner Tapan Bhanot is among the few senior officers continuing in Ludhiana.There has also been a churn at the executive engineer level. Sanjeev Sharma, who was posted in Bathinda, has been brought to Ludhiana as corporation engineer (civil), while Arvind Kumar has been transferred to Patiala and Raman Kaushal to Moga.Ranbir Singh, earlier posted in Jalandhar and holding additional charge of Phagwara, has been brought to Ludhiana as corporation engineer (O&M).In another key change, Surjit Singh Cheema will take over as municipal secretary of Ludhiana while also holding additional charge of Patiala.The building branch faces a vacancy at the top after the additional charge of Ludhiana held by Abohar municipal town planner Vijay Kumar was withdrawn. He will continue in Abohar, while no replacement for Ludhiana has been announced yet.The scale of the reshuffle puts the spotlight on continuity in civic works, particularly in the engineering and O&M wings. articles.title: JAC hikes fee for 2027 matric, intermediate exams; parents’ body seek review
articles.summary: JAC opens 2027 matric and intermediate exam applications, raises fees by Rs 120; matric Rs 1,100–1,300, intermediate Rs 1,220–1,520; parents seek review.
articles.body: Ranchi: The Jharkhand Academic Council (JAC) on Thursday opened the application process for the 2027 matric and intermediate examinations, with examination fees revised upward by Rs 120 for both categories compared to last year.Students can submit forms without a late fee until Nov 26. Under the revised structure, matric candidates will have to pay between Rs 1,100 and Rs 1,300, while intermediate students will be charged between Rs 1,220 and Rs 1,520, depending on category. JAC chairman Natwa Hansdak did not respond to TOI’s calls seeking his comment on the revised examination fees.JAC secretary S D Tigga said, “Students submitting forms within the regular window must deposit their examination fees by Nov 30. Those missing the deadline can apply with a late fee until Dec 4, with the corresponding fee payment to be completed by Dec 7.”On the examination schedule, Tigga said, “The board has not held a meeting yet to decide the examination dates. Tentatively, the examinations are expected to begin in the first week of Feb.”Around 8 lakh students are expected to appear for the matric and intermediate examinations combined in 2027. In 2026, over 7.48 lakh candidates registered for the two examinations, including 4,23,861 matric and 3,24,321 intermediate students.JAC has directed schools and colleges to download application forms, prepare the List of Students and verify entries against registration records to ensure that no eligible candidate is left out.The fee revision has added to concerns among some families. “For us, arranging the examination fee means setting aside a little money from daily earnings. We cannot always spare the entire amount at once, so we have to save in advance to ensure our child does not miss the application deadline or end up paying a late fee,” said Lakshman Mahato, a daily-wage labourer and parent of a Class 10 student.Ajay Rai, president of Jharkhand Abhibhavak Sangh, criticised JAC for the price hike and urged state govt to intervene. “Most govt school students come from labourer, farmer and lower middle-class households and may struggle to bear the additional burden. We demand review of the revised fee and restoration of the previous rates besides special concessions for financially disadvantaged students,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Brooklyn building collapse: 6 adults and 2 children dead, and 18 others injured, as rescuers search for survivors; pregnant woman pulled from rubble
articles.summary: At least seven children were among those injured after an apartment building in New York City collapsed Wednesday into a construction site.
articles.body:
At a press conference on Thursday afternoon, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani provided updates on the Brooklyn building collapse, saying that six adults and two children were among the eight people who died on Wednesday. Two of the adults who died were construction workers.

"This has been a devastating evening and morning for our city," Mamdani said.

Mamdani also confirmed that 18 other people were injured, including 14 civilians and four firefighters. The vast majority of those injured and being treated at hospitals are in stable condition, with one person in critical condition.

"I want to take a moment to remember those we have so senselessly lost. These were our friends and our neighbors, parents and children," the mayor said. "Young families building their lives in our city and immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador, Trinidad and beyond. Let us continue to hold close those who have been plunged into unimaginable grief and pray for a full and rapid recovery for every New Yorker injured."

Mamdani also thanked the first responders and construction workers who helped dig through the rubble to find survivors. "People are alive today because of their heroism yesterday," he said.

"Firefighters arrived on the scene in less than one minute after the 911 call first came in," Mamdani added.

The American Red Cross has opened a reception center at the Flatbush YMCA for residents who were affected and displaced by the building collapse. Mamdani said the city and American Red Cross will continue to provide "expanded services" from the Flatbush YMCA for residents displaced by the building collapse, including temporary housing, assistance with social services and mental health support.

"A tragedy of this magnitude demands a comprehensive and thorough investigation that includes both the construction site and the building which collapsed."

Mamdani said that the investigation has already begun, with law enforcement leading it. "There are five main entities involved with this construction site, or associated, with approximately 100 other sites across the city. Our Department of Buildings is commencing sweeps of those sites today."

FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said Thursday's rainstorm won't stop their operations at the collapse site. "It will definitely hinder our efforts, but this type of an emergency is something our members train extensively for and we will be here until we are one hundred percent sure there are no more people trapped," Bonsignore said.

"To be clear, we have not shifted from rescue to recovery. We are still in the search and rescue phase. We have moved into a general debris removal and we are using grapplers to move big chunks of the debris so we can search beneath them," Bonsignore added.

This is a developing story. Check back for updates. Read the original story below.

At least eight people died and 18 others were injured, when a three-story building collapsed Wednesday in the Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York.

The four-unit apartment building crumpled into a construction site next to it at about 4 p.m. ET.

Those who were injured were taken to a hospital and included four in critical condition, officials said. Seven were children and three were firefighters. Authorities did not confirm if any children were among those killed.

In a post on X Thursday morning , New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, "Rescue workers have spent the night searching the site of yesterday's building collapse, working under extremely dangerous conditions to find and save anyone who may still be trapped.

"I am heartbroken that eight New Yorkers have now lost their lives and at least 17 have been injured, including three firefighters. There are no words for a loss of this magnitude. My heart is with the families and loved ones of those we have lost, those who are injured and everyone grieving today."

Two deaths were announced on Wednesday, with six further deaths confirmed Thursday.

Water service was restored to about 100 buildings in the area on Thursday after the New York City Department of Environmental Protection had to shut down city water mains so that emergency crews could continue search and rescue operations, according to a post on X .

Rescuers searched for survivors into the night with about 250 first responders working at the scene. "We'll continue to look until we find everybody," FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said. A spokesperson for the FDNY told the New York Times Thursday that rescuers were still hoping to find survivors.

A pregnant woman was among those pulled out of the rubble. Footage broadcast by CBS News New York showed her being taken away on a stretcher more than two hours after the building collapsed, while her husband waited in anguish.

"She is alive. She is still alive. I'm very happy. I'm very happy. I'm very happy. I thank all of you guys," he told CBS News New York after she was rescued. "She's pregnant, six months."

Earlier, the man had been seen frantically looking for her. "I've heard nothing. She's inside the building. She's pregnant," he told reporters.

One resident, Anderson Velez, told the New York Post he was at work in the Bronx when his wife called him and said their children, ages 7 and 2, were trapped.

"She called me when the building collapsed while she was inside with rubble on top of her. She was screaming for someone to help get my son out and then the call cut off," he said, confirming his family was now safe.

An eyewitness, Melissa Orna, told the New York Times : "The whole building started shaking, and then it just fell."

The 1930s building fell into an adjoining construction site, where excavation work was ongoing. The cause of the collapse is under investigation, said John Esposito, the city's fire department chief. He said rescue teams may need to take several days to search the site for all potential victims.

Officials have described the search and rescue mission as "very dangerous," with firefighters and police officers punching holes through rubble in the search of survivors.

"Multiple people from the building and the construction site were trapped," Bonsignore said. "This will be a prolonged operation. Collapse operations are extremely dangerous. Every move is choreographed and critically important to patient outcomes and member safety. Members have been working methodically and haven't stopped since they arrived."

No official cause for the collapse has been released.

In April, the New York City Department of Buildings issued a violation to a demolition contractor at the construction site who "unlawfully continued work while on notice of a Stop Work Order," according to the violation. Inspectors noted that a single-story building was demolished despite the city's order to stop work. The violation was resolved in October, according to DOB records .

Yahoo has requested comment from the DOB about why the city ordered a work stoppage in the first place.

On Wednesday, DOB issued a full stop work order "due to unsafe construction operations causing adjacent building (1321 Flatbush Avenue) to collapse."

Mamdani said at a news conference Wednesday that rescue workers arrived on the scene within one minute of receiving the 911 call. He also confirmed some of the fatalities and said that injured people had been transported to local hospitals.

"This has been an incredibly challenging and fast-moving situation — with precarious wreckage to navigate and dangerous voids beneath the surface," he said, adding, "This type of rescue is exactly what the FDNY trains for."

He also asked New Yorkers to "please take a moment to pray for those who passed away today and all of those who are mourning their loss."
